Starting small, in my opinion, is really the only way to go. I didn't one day just decide to spend a couple hundred dollars on supplies for a hobby. I started with a small setup because I thought it would be cool. Then I bought a couple of plants, upgraded my setup, discovered a related craft, and have been gradually collecting everything I need to create my ideal project. The same goes for my vehicle. I have a friend, on the other hand, who spends a lot of money on a hobby and then quits after a month or so. A few months back, he told me and another friend that he was getting into a craft. A couple of weeks later, I asked if he had made anything, and he said, "nah, I need to buy more tools first." How can you invest so much in a hobby that you only like the idea of? He has no idea if he will even enjoy that craft.

I feel like planted tanks can get equally or more complex than saltwater (although admittedly I know near nothing of saltwater tanks) with light levels, light spectrums, CO2 systems, and conditions to breed different fish and invertebrates. If someone told me three years ago that setting up a fish tank is a form of art, I would roll my eyes, but it totally is, and it's almost the only form of artistic expression that I really enjoy. I'm creating a little underwater world in which different creatures will interact. Then after the initial planting, you get to watch it all grow out. You kind of set it up not in a way that looks super awesome, but in a way that will look super awesome when all of your plants start thriving.
